question: Quit to build?
dilemma: I'm thinking about quitting my PM job to build an AI tool that chases late invoices for freelancers. I have about 9 months of savings, but I'm scared of giving up a steady paycheck.

options.label: Keep job, build on the side

cruxes.statement: Most freelancers would pay $15 a month
I can live on an unstable income
I can make real progress in 10 hours a week
Freedom matters more to me than a steady paycheck

experiments.title: Ask 5 freelancers to pay $15 a month
steps: Message 5 freelancers you know or find in communities
Ask how they handle late invoices today
Show the one-line pitch and the $15 price
Ask: "Would you pay for this next month?"
experiments.sensitivityReason: If most say no, quitting to build this would be a guess.

measure.question: Would you pay for this next month?

experiments.title: Live on 40% of your salary for a month
steps: Move 60% of each paycheck to savings on payday
Note the days you went over
experiments.sensitivityReason: Shows whether a smaller income is livable before it's real.

experiments.title: Walk through a day in month 8
experiments.sensitivityReason: Shows what you care about, not what will happen.

moments.text: No alarm, no morning meeting. You open your laptop at the kitchen table. A few early customers. Not much income.
One of your first customers asks for a refund: "My accounting app already sends reminders."
choices: Refund, and ask what would make it worth paying for
Offer a free month to keep them

moments.text: Your old team posts a photo. The project you started is finished, without you.
You check your bank app. One month of savings left. Rent is due Friday.

experiments.title: Research startup failure rates
experiments.sensitivityReason: General statistics don't say anything about this idea.

experiments.title: Quit for a month to see how it feels
experiments.sensitivityReason: Would answer the question, but can't be undone.

experiments.title: Keep your job and chase invoices by hand for 3 freelancers for two weeks
steps: Find 3 freelancers with an overdue invoice
Send reminders for them for two weeks
Track hours spent and whether they'd pay to keep it going
experiments.sensitivityReason: Tests Path B, which has no evidence yet, and whether people will pay for help.

measure.question: Would you pay to keep this going?

evidence.transcript: Four of them hate chasing invoices, but only one would actually pay. Two said their accounting app already sends reminders.
